utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that he was the top man there and that he must have been a member of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you don't know about that specifically?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then I'm not going to show you that document -- or rather, you said that he was a member of the SPO, you know that for sure?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 5 you say that you know that Arsen Grahovac met up with Seselj in Belgrade. How come that is in your statement?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From who?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people who were on the front line with me, excuse me, in Mostar. And they were from Mostar you see, but I do not believe anything I don't see myself. These are various tales.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But these tales became part of your statement. What are we going to do about it now?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that's what I heard about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mention here that you heard that Seselj's volunteers were in Mostar, there were about 50 of them; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard, that they were up there at the garrison command, but I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 9 on page 4, you say that Seselj's men came to Buna and that the commander of Seselj's men was a local man known as Bovan.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, Dr. Seselj. I moved from Zalik to the Zvezda Cinema in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you say that he was a member of the SDS and the president of SDS for Buna?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come Seselj's men could be under his command then?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know -- oh, but it was -- it is correct that he was a member --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come you mention Seselj's men here?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right then. Perhaps the OTP just interjected that there without you seeing it or knowing about it.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. If it's quite possible, let's move on. They quote later on that you saw a check-point that was manned by Seselj's men, which is what you stated in your first statement; and then you explain here that there were Seselj's men from Serbia there and that some man called Kinez was there commander, that he had a uniform similar to Croatian uniforms, et cetera. Is that what you explained there?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said already that when coming to Mostar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Witness. I thought that Mr. Seselj was going to ask you more questions about the contents of the statement regarding Seselj's men. You stated that there was a group that committed crimes and you mentioned various places, Kula, Buna, Mostar, Bijelo Polje, Pisevce [phoen]. And you went on to say that they committed the crimes in the village of Sopilja, where some hundred people were killed. You added this: In Mostar there was another Chetnik unit of some 50 men. They wore Chetnik insignia and then in brackets there is cockades, the two-head eagles, et cetera. And then you continued. You said: "We knew that they were always Seselj's volunteers from Serbia. This unit didn't have any specific name," you said. So what you say is very serious and very specific. You said that there was a 100-men-strong unit which you described, and you said that these were people from Serbia, Seselj's volunteers. This is written in your statement. And beforehand you said that they committed crimes. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you nicely that I remember and that I know that in the garrison command there was a group of volunteers known as Seseljevci. Now, that they had committed crimes in town or around it, I'm not aware of that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you said that they came from Serbia. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learnt that as we held the eastern part of the town and there was a front line there and we moved around town, and I learned from men who were close to the garrison command. But I myself never went to that command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I'm not mistaken, yesterday you also said that they spoke differently from the locals. Do I remember properly or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you're not mistaken. They spoke the Ekavica dialect. You know what Ekavica is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One detail. My colleagues and I were really sort of poring over this statement, and it appears that there were two groups. There was those who committed the crimes in Nevesinje, where over 100 people were killed, and then there is a full stop in the sentence in your statement. Then the sentence went on, and it is said that in Mostar there is another Chetnik group of some 50 people. And apparently it was this group that was made up of volunteers, Serbian volunteers, from Serbia. So given the way the sentence is written, one could infer that the group that committed crimes was not Seselj's group. But the sentence is supposed to render what you said to Ms. St. Germain. So you are the only one who could tell us whether there were indeed two groups, which one was it that did, and what they did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, while I was in Mostar and while I moved around the area where we were functioning, I said that I did not see a single volunteer or member of the Serbian Radical Party that are known as Seseljevci. As for the crimes and the pits and these killings in Nevesinje and the municipality of Nevesinje, I heard about them in hospital and when I returned from hospital. So I was in hospital from the 13th of June until the 1st of August, and all this was happening while I was in hospital. So what can I say? I can just say that I heard about these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you heard about it. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What does this mean in paragraph 15, that you were in the Mostar unit before you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the territorial defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here it says Mostarska unit. Maybe it's a misinterpretation. Did you say Mostarska unit.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostarska unit. We were protecting the bridge. And that's why they translated it as the bridge unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 15 you say during the period that I spent in my bridge unit, I never saw any crimes committed by members of the Seseljevci. Then you mention a Vranjanac, you say that he was one of the Seseljevci, that you never met him, and that you do not know that he committed any crime. So before your wounding, you clearly said that you were not aware of a single crime committed by the Seseljevci.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there I didn't see nor did I hear -- Dr. Seselj, I repeat, I never saw a single man of yours down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But then it says here that you heard of the Seseljevci crimes while you were in Montenegro in hospital. Did you hear in Montenegro in the hospital that Seseljevci had committed crimes?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 10 or 15 of us there from the Nevesinje brigade and from Mostar, so I didn't hear anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You speak about the participation of Seseljevci and Red Berets in the attack on Bijelo Polje on the 19th of May. Are you sure that the Seseljevci and the Red Berets were acting together?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I came to Mostar after the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Then in paragraph 17 there is reference to the crime in Uborak, in Gornji Vrapcici, and you say here that you don't know whether Seseljevci or the Red Berets were involved, but you do say that the Seseljevci were under Kandic's control. Kandic was the commander of a battalion in the Nevesinje Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was but very briefly, for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you're talking about Ratko Kandic, he was killed in the war?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They say that he was a great hero during the war; is that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And was he in this area where General Glusic says that members of the Serbian Radical Party were involved? When you mentioned Klepci?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there I didn't see Kandic at all. Where did you find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it says here in your statement that he was in command of the Seseljevci.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So that's not true, is it? Now we come to the best bit, that's paragraph 20, and here you're quoted from your first statement. There were about 100 Seselj's men and about 50 armed volunteers. They were never issued any military cards nor were they registered, so referring to the 50 and not the Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We just saw that there weren't a hundred but 19 plus one, 20. You saw General Glusic's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the witness that statement by the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here that you said allegedly: "I wish to add the following. During the summer of 1993" --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, what statement is Mr. Seselj referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Statement of 2004, paragraph 20, there's no numbered paragraph in the statement of 2000. The statement of 2000 is not divided into paragraphs, whereas the statement of 2004 is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ms. Biersay, to make things easier, if I understand Mr. Seselj he's reading the 2004 statement and you see this was done by your own investigators. They numbered the paragraphs. We're now dealing with paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I understand that. I thought I heard the interpretation as please give the witness the statement from the general. So that's when I stood up to ask what statement of the general are we talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the usher to be kind enough to give the general certificate back to me which was on the ELMO so that it doesn't get lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now you're allegedly adding here, first of all when you referred to Seselj's men in the first statement it referred to the year 1992, but here you say: "I want to add the following. During the summer of 1993 these men came to Nevesinje on two buses from Serbia. They were members of the Serb Volunteer Guard (meaning Seseljevci) and members of the SPO party led by Vuk Draskovic. They had photographs of Vojislav Seselj and Vuk Draskovic on the buses. Their commander was Zvonko Osmajlic. He later got killed. At one point he was Vuk Draskovic's body-guard. When they arrived they joined with the Red Berets and the 2nd Light Brigade which was a JNA brigade, and their commander at that point was Boro Antelj. The deputy commander of Osmajlic was Branislav Lainovic." So this was science fiction. This would not be possible in a cartoon. Did you say this or did somebody put this in your statement without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Vojislav Seselj, my position was 35 kilometres away from Nevesinje, so I heard from people who came up there, as we worked in shifts, that they had seen two buses coming of these volunteers of the guard of the SPO, the Serbian Renewal Movement, they were led by Osmajlic and apparently there were some of yours and Vuk Draskovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed slowly, though this will take some time. It says here they were members of the Serb Volunteer Guard (i.e. Seseljevci). Can under any conditions members of the Serbian Volunteer Guard be called Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, how could they?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you did call them that here.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I heard this up on the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear at the front that members of the Serb volunteer guard were Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, who said that, people who came to take over as the next shift?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you a moment ago that I don't believe anything I don't see. I didn't see any of this. I just heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but you didn't say that here. You're giving a statement to the Prosecution which is incriminating me. I simply can't stop wondering how I can read something like this in your statement. And let me tell you something else, the name isn't good, the Serb Volunteer Guard was held by Arkan and Draskovic had the Serbian guards. This is a minor difference in the name, but every Serb was aware of the difference, of the distinction.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know what a fierce conflict there was between the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Renewal Party, between me and Vuk Draskovic in 1993 as it says here?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that you were in conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. There was an absolute conflict between us.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I hear this from you for the first time. I didn't have any media available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could it be possible that photographs of Vojislav Seselj and Vuk Draskovic be posted next to one another on buses in the summer of 1993? How is that possible? And their commander was Zvonko Osmajlic. Could you explain that to me, did somebody tell you this on the front?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, because I was at the command post and that is where the shifts took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And so they told you that these two photographs were stuck together on the buses and they went off to the Borac Lake and that Zvonko Osmajlic was the commander. The commander of the Seseljevci of all the people in the buses. Were there any Seseljevci in those buses?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could you make such a statement? Did you see this when you signed this?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the statements I signed were written in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but you confirm now that you had heard that Seseljevci were members of the Serb volunteer guard. Judge Antonetti asked you something yesterday. He asked you whether it is the same Vuk Draskovic who was the foreign minister, and you said no, that it was somebody else. And I was astonished to hear this. Do you know that Vuk Draskovic, president of the Serbian Renewal Movement and the founder of the Serbian Guards, was the minister for foreign affairs, first of Serbia and Montenegro and later of Serbia only. Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it and saw it on television. I didn't say it was him. This was some other Vuk Draskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So someone else was a minister?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't a minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The minister now is Vuk Jeremic. Maybe you mixed up the two names, Vuk Jeremic and Vuk Draskovic. But you never heard that Vuk Draskovic was the foreign minister?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I know that he was the minister, but I'm saying that he wasn't there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said yesterday that he was at the Borac lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, no, no, nobody said that. The judge didn't say that that he was at the Borac lake, but the Judge asked you when you were talking about Draskovic's guards, whether it was the same Draskovic that was the foreign minister. Maybe you didn't understand the question. Did -- do you know that the French president at the time, Francois Miterrand in 1993, when the Serb -- Draskovic's Serb guards were fighting at the Borac lake, that President Miterrand invited Vuk Draskovic and his wife Danica for treatment to France and recovery, because they were arrested during bloodshed, during some demonstrations when they were beaten up. That is what the Judge asked you. Had you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear of it from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On all the Serb media published it that Carla del Ponte, while she was the lead Prosecutor, publicly acclaimed Vuk Draskovic and praised him while he was foreign minister as her best friend and ally in Belgrade. Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you hear Vuk Draskovic fiercely advocating the delivery of Ratko Mladic and Hadzic to The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear that from you and I believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Ratko Mladic should be held responsible for the crimes committed by his followers in Herzegovina and now he wants him arrested, and the Serb people won't give Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is the whole of the Serbian people very proud of Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, 1.000 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The entire Serb people are proud of Ratko Mladic 1.000 per cent. And here they've accused Ratko Mladic even of the crimes committed by Draskovic; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us move on. In paragraph 21 they are quoting what you said in your first statement where there is no mention of Seselj's men, the crime, the massacre in Teleca Lastva, and now you add that Seseljevci and the Red Berets were responsible for it. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in that paragraph that it says very nicely that the only thing that I do know, that is to say what I heard, happened at the time when I was wounded; namely, that Seselj's men and the Red Berets were responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men from the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come Seseljevci were at Teleca Lastva?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was surprised by that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I know, but --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had already left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But what you add here is: The only thing I know about this incident, Teleca Lastva massacre, is the fact that the Seseljevci and Red Berets were responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now I'm answering --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Judges can't wait to impose a life sentence on me on the basis of this, what you say you hadn't even seen yourself, that you heard sort of from someone.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I was in hospital at the time and I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who were at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who talked about that, people at the barber shop? Who, what?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard it from my fellow combatants.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that in your first statement to the OTP because that is a very important piece of information. Had you said that in your first statement, maybe you would have convinced me too; however, since that is not in your first statement but only in the second one that was tendentiously prepared in 2004 for my trial, you keep adding Red Berets, Seseljevci, Red Berets, Seseljevci, look at paragraph 22 as well. And then in paragraph 25: "Seselj's volunteers were members of the Karadjordje group and Arsen Grahovac was their leader." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have two comments. First an assumption. If you had died, the Prosecutor would have tendered your statement under Rule 92 quater. This is the procedure that we use here. When someone is deceased, his or her statement may be tendered through this rule, and I'm sure you understand the consequences. In 2004 when Mr. Yves Roy contacted you. I've never met this man. I don't know who it is. He takes all the paragraphs that you had in your 2000 statement and reviews them, but systematically he always adds something. Each time there is written: I said, and then information that you add. So any trier of fact reading this could think that this witness is extremely accurate because every time he says "I said," and the entire statement is organised in such a way. So everything is very -- very specific, very precise, but it seems that now you're telling us that this is all hearsay, that everything that is written is hearsay. So you should have said -- you should have told Mr. Roy: I am saying this because I heard it from someone else. Furthermore, on paragraph 2, because they there are paragraph numbers, paragraph 2 for this Karadjordje group and Grahovac's group, you say he was a member of the SRS in Nevesinje. This is exactly what you're saying. And when you said that you were absolutely sure that Grahovac was a member of the SRS in Nevesinje and that they -- and that the SRS had a local structure there with politicians who took part in elections, with a local president for the party in that place, and so forth and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, I certainly wasn't sure of that, but I was sure that this was a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement, but I wanted to tell you something about what you had said: How come you never said that during that questioning? Well, the person who was putting questions to me did not even ask me whether I had heard about that or this or that. Do you understand what I'm saying? Most of these things that had happened, happened during that period of time when I was in hospital. And when I got out of hospital, I do not remember that there was any massacre anywhere or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, fine, fine. You said he was member of the Serbian Renewal Party, but this is not the Serbian Radical Party. It's not the same thing. The investigator maybe was confused and didn't understand and would write SRS and not think twice about it, fine, that might have happened. But, you see, there are consequences. Imagine you had died. This document would be binding and any Judge reading this would see Grahovac was a member of the Serbian Radical Party period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I told you yesterday very nicely that I'm not quite sure -- actually, I mean -- well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me read this sentence. "The only Chetnik group present was the group of Arsen Grahovac called Karadjordje. He was a member of the SRS in Nevesinje, he was there with his group of 20 to 30 men." That is the sentence as it is written in English. So when reading this anyone can infer that Grahovac is a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If I may intervene at this point and assist in refreshing the Presiding Judge's memory, I think we covered this issue yesterday when I was you putting my questions to the witness, and it became clear that this statement made by the witness in paragraph 2 of the 2004 statement was indeed a mistake. So that has been clarified. The witness has confirmed today that at no point did he wish to maintain that Arsen Grahovac was a member of the SRS. The witness has repeatedly highlighted that Mr. Grahovac, as far as he knew, was a member of the SPO. So I think we can stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. Harhoff, look at paragraph 25, the last sentence. It says: "The Seseljevci volunteers were members of the Karadjordje group and their leader was Arsen Grahovac." You see what kind of a mess we're dealing with here and how do we get out of it? All of this was added on to the statement of 2000. They were inserting things there because they issued an indictment against me when there was no evidence whatsoever, and then they fabricated this kind of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, in that same paragraph if you go up a few lines it appears that what is reflected here is what the witness heard in the third line, at least in the English version, it says that he heard that the Red Berets, the SPO members, and the Seseljevci were involved in these killings. But it's clear that this is something that he heard, and I don't think that we can take it any further than that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Harhoff, if the witness had heard something, he should tell us as a bare minimum I think who he heard it from. If it was women at the barber shop who were talking about that, he has to say which woman was having a shave and talked about that. So I want to hear from the witness who it was that was saying that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You have heard from the witness. He told you that he had heard this from combatants who had been at the front line and who had come back that he met.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I have yet another question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since you did not hear that from the fighters who came back from the front line before your statement in 2000, that means that you heard all of this about Seseljevci between 2000 and 2004; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I did not hear about it from fellow combatants who had come from the front line, but rather from those who were going to the front line, Dr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, so you heard it from those who were about to go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who had come from Nevesinje that was 35 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now I'm even more confused. Instead of hearing about Seselj's men who were criminals from people who came from the front line where crimes were being committed, you heard that from people who were yet to go there; that is to say, that they went there with certain information to the effect that Seselj's men were committing crimes in some kind of impossible combination with members of the SPO and the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as you said a few moments ago, I mean, you know, women in a barber shop, I can just add one more thing that women at the market-place in Nevesinje knew a lot more. Perhaps the Court is not really interested in that but they knew more than we did at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So did you learn something from women at the market-place?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, all sorts of things. Like, tomorrow there's going to be an attack on Mostar and whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, on page 28 you say: "I want to add the following. The killings in Gacko that happened around the 20th of June, 1992, were committed by the Red Berets Seseljevci, Serbs from Gacko, Bileca, et cetera," what does that mean? How come Seseljevci were in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that period I really wasn't there and -- I mean I was in hospital. I heard that in hospital in Meljine from these wounded men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Obviously, the investigators who were speaking to you in 2004, they kept insisting on you inserting "Seselj's men" into your statement? Did they insist on that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a large part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they offer anything in return?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what, in return that would mean, well, that some third country was offered to me, that I was paid per diems for having skipped work, then my travel expenses, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then it turned out to be a lie, what they told you about the third country?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 2000 was a long time ago and now it's been ten years, right, and you can see that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they lied to you. But I want you to tell me whether it's true, then you say, yes, it's true, they lied to me. I mean, it's not that I want to get this out of you. Did they lie to you?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. So when you realised that they were lying to you, then you turned to my associates and you asked to come and testify as a Defence witness. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. So that is a full answer on your part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, but I should mention it and how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Seselj, but I have a question for the witness. Witness, you understood that they lied while they were telling you all this, or did you just understand today that they lied at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know how it was. During the first talks a promise was made to me that I would leave very shortly. That was at the first interview and the second and the third interview. So it wasn't a short-term dead-line. Short-term is five or ten days, so it's not just some ordinary statement. It is practically a military secret, highly confidential. It's not easy to say that kind of thing. You know how people look at you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I don't understand your answer. You said that you understood that they lied. I would like to know whether you understood that they lied when they were actually telling you all these, all this, or did -- or is it just today that you finally understood that they lied? When did you understand that they were lying? Who exactly is "they"? Is it the OTP, the soldiers, the combatants? The combatants, the people who told you all these things. You understood that when they were telling you all this, actually they were telling you a bunch of lies? Very well. Now, I would like to know exactly when you understood that they were lying, at what point in time. Was it at the time, while they were telling you all these lies or just today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like an answer from the witness before you speak, Mr. Seselj. After I have my answer, you can say whatever you want, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I thought that you were asking ant the interview with Ms. Brigitte. Do you understand me? That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. We've already talked about this at length yesterday. We've understood that there was an interpreter, that the interpreter read you a number of things. You even said that the interpreter changed things. This has settled the matter. I'm talking about something else. Now, have you understood my question this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat your question, but briefly, briefly. I went to the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat slowly. In these statements you're saying a number of things about Seselj's volunteers who would have done this -- this or that, but you add that you heard this only through hearsay. And you also added who told you about this, so who was responsible for this hearsay. But then later you said that you understood that when these people were telling you all these things they were just telling you a bunch of lies. It seems that now that there were just liars everywhere. Fine. Set this aside, but this is what you said. Now, I would like to know when exactly you understood, you realised, that these were lies, that all these people who were telling you all these things were liars. Was it as they -- when they were telling you all the lies or did you find -- realise this now, today, finally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madame Judge, I said that I do not believe anything until I see it. I heard everything they said, what was going on, and how it went on. I said what I knew. Had you asked me about something that I had seen for myself at the front line, I would have confirmed all of that for you. Basically, I didn't believe anything coming from anyone. I really did hear a lot of lies. How should I put this to you? Well, I will give you an example. I was a soldier. I was involved in shooting. I'm not hiding that. So I kill someone for instance and they say, "He didn't do it, somebody else did it," so it is hearsay. That's what we call it in our language. So that's the same thing what happened. They wanted -- they wanted to blame someone else. They wanted to blame someone who was well-known, like the members of the Serb Radical Party or Seselj's volunteers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, you understood that they were lying at the time, when they were telling you all those lies, you knew that they were lies, you had realised that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 99 per cent I was convinced because I didn't believe these things, I didn't see them, I just heard about them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you did not share what you were convinced with the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Prosecutor didn't ask me that at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something now, Judge Lattanzi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I'm addressing you now. You started this discussion with the witness after I had discussed with him for some time about his conversations with The Hague investigators, and the witness confirmed that The Hague investigators had asked him to amend his previous statement and add the Seseljevci. And then I asked him: What did they offer in return? And the witness said: They offered me life in a foreign country. My question then was: Did they lie to you? And the witness said: Yes. And I insisted that he give me a clear-cut answer whether they had lied to him. So the witness wasn't saying that the people who were telling him about the crimes of the Seseljevci, but it was The Hague investigators who lied to him because they offered him life in a foreign country. And when he signed this statement, that was filled in with the Seseljevci everywhere. Nothing came of it. And then, realising that he had been lied to and as a sign of revolt, he addressed my Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this is something else, but thank you, but this is something completely different. I had fully understood and heard what was said about the so-called tampering that might have happened -- allegedly would have been done by the Prosecutor. But this witness also talked about people, women, all sorts of people who told them this and that, that he had understood that these were lies. And this is what my question was about, about these facts. I wanted to know when he realised that these were lies. And I understood now that he realised it at the time but he did not convey that to the Prosecutor because he never denied not having said this to the Prosecutor. As to the reasons why he said what he said, well the Trial Chamber will see into that. But he never denied that he had said this to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned here the Red Berets, but you said yesterday that they were not the Red Berets belonging to the police of Serbia from a later date, but that they are Red Berets from the 2nd Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They organised themselves on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Boro Antelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But Captain Boro Antelj was the commander of this light brigade, right? But who was the commander of the Red Beret units within that brigade?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baca Milosevic who left the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Baca Milosevic, I see. I was given a document by the Prosecution which comes from the military security service of Croatia, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, forward command post Posusje.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be kind enough to put this on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is the document dated the 30th of November, 1993. So let us briefly take a look at this document and could you comment on it, please. I would like us to identify who these people are. You've already said this is a unit within the brigade. Let us see what it says for the Baca, what the Croats say. Here it is. You see, this is an interview with a representative of the VRS, and they say that on the 29th of November they had an interview with Baca Milosevic, commander of special unit of the VRS, the so-called Red Berets. Also present was a member of the SIS, that is their security service, and Nikola Peric. In this document - and the Prosecution has this document - they say that Baca Milosevic went to Mostar to Croatian territory. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he discussed co-operation between Serbian and Croatian forces in the struggle against Muslim forces, and they even considered the possibility of jointly taking Konjic in the third paragraph, the town of Konjic. You see that? And that is the only reason we need this document. So the Croats also knew that this was a special unit of the VRS, the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Has this unit any connection with Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. There's no connection. And never during the armed conflict did I go to Borac lake, and I can assert that this unit had only one operation that was just an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So we're not interested in that. So within the framework of that light Konjic brigade, there was this unit called the Red Berets and Baca Milosevic was in command. Was that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And was there Arsen Grahovac's unit, Karadjordje, until he was killed?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And was there the Serbian Guards from Serbia sent by Vuk Draskovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Under the commander Zoran Osmajlic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the rest of the unit were locally mobilised soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Main Staff of Republika Srpska from 1994 did everything they could to get rid of Boro Antelj, did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I believe you because I know more or less why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me so that they don't think I'm leading you. But why did they wish to dismiss him?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in the period of 1993 in my assessment there was an impermissible trade with the Croatian army from the small place of Turija near Konjic inhabited by Croats, and there was a re-settlement of Croats across Serb territory. Then fuel was brought in from Kiseljak for the Croatian army, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you're talking about smuggling?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know that he provided military weapons to the Serbian Renewal Movement in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear of that for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. If you hadn't heard about it I won't insist.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have this document back, Mr. Usher. Your Honours, did you plan a break now or shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, it's time for the break. We will break for 20 minutes. I believe you have about 30 minutes left. The Registrar will check this for us and I'll tell you when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court is back in session. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There is something else I was surprised by, Mr. Dabic. When you were talking about these two rallies of the Serbian Democratic Party in Mostar and Nevesinje, you said that they were held in 1991; is that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but you said in 1991. The rallies that you spoke about were held in 1990, prior to the first multi-party elections; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in 1990 Arsen Grahovac didn't have any armed groups?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this occurred in July 1991, a year later?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see you properly because of the ELMO, please, because of this antenna.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you remove the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We're wasting time. There are quite a number of things I'd like to clear up. Did you make a mistake there unconsciously or what -- in connection -- in connection with these rallies in Mostar and Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought it was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in 1990 nobody was armed, were they? In 1991, yes; but in 1990 no; am I right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I see you have to correct that, too?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned my coming to Nevesinje in 1995. In paragraph 29 of this second statement of 2004. You say here that: "I came with two military trucks, three or four cars with Belgrade plates, and with the flag of the Serbian Radical Party," is that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that what you saw?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But how come this is in your statement?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the four years that I was on the front, I spent only three months in Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you see this on television then?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any TV. I lived in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 29 you describe my coming to Nevesinje in 1995, and in paragraph 30 you say that this event was shown on Trebinje TV a few days later. And now you're say that you didn't have a TV and that you couldn't have watched this.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 30th paragraph I didn't say this. My name is not mentioned there, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Your name isn't mentioned, but there's your signature at the end of the statement.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you know about Radovan Radovic, he was killed. He was the commander of a special unit that rallied volunteers from the area of Bileca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This was a unit that fought heroically at many fronts?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Radovan Radovic is considered a great hero among the Serb people; am I right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that Radovan Radovic was involved in a war crime ever?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not, and there isn't a battle front in Bosnia and Herzegovina where he wasn't -- where he was present and me being present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So what I'm asking is: You're not aware of a single crime that Radovan Radovic was involved in. Do you know that Radovan Radovic in 1994 joined the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you know that after he became a member I proclaimed him a Serbian Chetnik Vojvoda?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that you had proclaimed him Vojvoda, but I didn't hear that he was proclaimed a Chetnik Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I can only proclaim Chetnik Vojvodas and no others.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that is what I did but only once he had joined the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that he had become a member, but I did know that he was a Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know how many people I proclaimed Serbian Chetnik Vojvodas from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know of the late Radovan Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Had you heard of Nedeljko Vidakovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear it from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He is from Trebinje who had a unit of local volunteers, and he fought in the direction of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the Trebinje battle front only when Knin fell. And Vidakovic was killed as a hero during the war. I hear that from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: These are the only two Serbian Chetnik Vojvodas that I proclaimed from Herzegovina, but you only heard of Radovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who did you hear from about my coming to Nevesinje? Did you tell the investigator this or did he write it himself?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that I spent very little time in Nevesinje, and I heard about this when I came for a bath to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my co-combatants who were living in the barracks. We didn't have a home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you said here that I came with three or four cars with Belgrade plates and the flag of the Serbian Radical Party at the head of the column. This is what you heard?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And with us there were two military trucks. Did those military trucks have Belgrade plates?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people told me that they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were they trucks of Radovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I went with them to the front line; is that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you say that from Nevesinje I went to Prijeka Grma. To tell you the truth, I don't remember this place, but probably that's true. That was the forward command post of the Nevesinje Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is 12 or 13 kilometres towards Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the commander was Zoran Purkovic, and you said that Zdravko Kandic was a major and an operative of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who did I meet with there, with Purkovic or Kandic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had heard I would have said, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you heard that I went to the front line with Radovan Radovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijeka Grma is not the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How far is the front line that I went to from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 kilometres, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 30 kilometres. That is where I went?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, let me tell you now exactly. Mostar-Nevesinje is 45 kilometres, about 37 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where I was at the front line, I was 37 kilometres from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you say here that there was a tank there, that a soldier asked me to get in, but I couldn't get in because you say I was too fat for the tank?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you say that I was too fat?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I heard about these things. I didn't see you; if I had, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does any army in the world manufacture tanks for 2-metre high people like me? It's always shorter soldiers are chosen for -- to man a tank. Have you ever seen a tank operator of 2 metres?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only basketball players are that high.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I could never be a tank driver. So then you say that I took a Browning machine-gun and fired at Mostar. Did you say that? In paragraph 29, last sentence: "Instead of that he took a Browning machine-gun and fired at Mostar."

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep telling you I told them what I heard. I never saw you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did I open fire at Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I know when I didn't see you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But that is what it says here, that I took a Browning machine-gun and fired at Mostar. Is a Browning fixed on a tank?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's 12.7-calibre and it's not mounted on a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What is the range of a machine-gun 12.7-calibre?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That would be a maximum, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If an ordinary machine-gun has a range of 2, then this one 3. But this line was 37 kilometres from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then how could I use a Browning machine-gun to fire at Mostar? I could have fired at the moon; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why does it say here that I was firing at Mostar? So has this been put in by the investigator to say that I fired at random to kill civilians in Mostar, but I was firing in the direction of Muslim positions not Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe you could have reached the Muslim lines either because they were too far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I had a howitzer of 203-millimetres, I couldn't have fired at Mostar either?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A 203-millimetre howitzer has a range of 20 kilometres, so I couldn't have fired at Mostar. Now, why does it say that here then? I can't understand this nonsense in this statement. How did it get in your statement? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This really was a long time ago, but I tell you that I remember talking in the barracks. But this conversation was much -- was much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me make myself clear. I'm proud of my role in this war. It was a small role, but I'm proud of it. I did visit Radovan Radovic's unit at the front line. I did open fire with a Browning machine, but not at Mostar. How can I fire at Mostar when it's 37 kilometres away? What about the moon, do you know how far the moon is? No, you don't know?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an astronomist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's easier to target the moon than Mostar because you can't see Mostar from this spot?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible. It is impossible to see it from Prijeka Grma.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there a mountain in front of us?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's a hill, there's a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you can't see anything in the direction of Mostar, can you?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were the Muslim positions on the hill?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I couldn't see anything behind that hill; is that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution could have found that clip because it was aired on television, and then they could see where I fired from and at what. We have mentioned Radovan Radovic. Do you know that the Chetnik Vojvoda Radovan Radovic was killed from the behind in January in Bileca?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. He killed him from behind and he was convicted to only two and a half years of imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, and he hid in Belgrade, and I think he served for about one year and nine months. And do you know that this same Krsto Savic was convicted at the state court of Bosnia and Herzegovina to 20 years of imprisonment for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have this judgement on a hundred pages. Whether it's founded on true facts or not, I haven't analysed it. The appeal ruling hasn't been made, but I know that Krsto Savic killed Radovan Radovic for no reason and that he was never properly punished for it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said yesterday that there were people who falsely claimed to be Serb Radicals. Were there some gangs that would be formed of who knows which bandits and would claim to be members of the Serb Radical --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Judge Lattanzi, have I made a mistake? The witness said yesterday that there were people who falsely claimed to be Serb Radicals --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's before --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour. Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not testifying. I'm just asking questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said that yesterday. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that today in Republika Srpska there's an entire political party that claims to be falsely a Serbian Radical Party led by somebody called Milenko Mihaljica.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear this from you because I rarely go to Republika Srpska or Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There's a party that has been in existence for seven years that is falsely claiming to be the Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska. With the help of the regime at the time, they took --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Objection. Mr. Seselj is speaking about things that have no relevance and his purpose is simply to use this as a public platform. And the Prosecution objects to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you told us that there is a Serbian Radical Party in the Republika Srpska that is not yours. We have understood what you meant to say. Please move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that is an important argument that supports the statement made by this witness yesterday, Mr. President. But all right, I'll move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your statement here you mentioned some other men whose names I find interesting. You mentioned Petar Divjakovic, Radovan Soldo, Dragan Zirojevic, and some others; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember having mentioned them?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, these men belonged to this so-called unit of the Red Berets at lake Borac; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I received information from Ilija Vuckovic, who was commander of the special-purpose unit of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska Krajina in the period from 1991 to 1993. It was in Pajzos near Ilok in the Republic of Serbian Krajina that his unit had its headquarters. Have you heard of that place?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You didn't hear of it before?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He says that in mid-1991 Petar Divjakovic and three other men, Dragan Zirojevic, Radovan Soldo, and the third name he cannot remember, joined that unit voluntarily and arrived there. That they spent 17 days in that unit and they trained and then fled from the unit and took their combat kits along. They had red berets on their heads. They also stole a van in the village of Lezimir near Sremska Mitrovica. The -- this was the property of a company from Lezimir. Do you know that they arrived in Mostar in that van?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear it from you, and also that they fled and how they got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then they appeared in that unit and through some false witnesses the Prosecution is trying to link them to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, objection. The witness said he heard this for the first time, and Mr. Seselj continued basically throwing false allegations and testifying, and we object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that you received a report from the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska about Krajina in 1992 or 1993, but the witness said "I don't know." So there's no point in insisting because he told you that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then I won't go on insisting. What Ms. Biersay says, that I am lying, I mean all the lies here come from the OTP starting with the false indictment --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection, objection Your Honour. That was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we had a lot of false statements here, false witnesses, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please do not make accusations. You have to prove that what you're saying is the truth. So before reaching any conclusions, you have to make your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your first statement on page 35 you mentioned the arrival of Radovan Karadzic in December 1994, he arrived in Nevesinje, then that's what you say, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, then you said that in Nevesinje Karadzic was not warmly welcomed and that they didn't really like him very much over there. His visit - and now they use these Croat words here, expressions that you do not use at all. Was that because Nevesinje was a stronghold of the SPO, is that why they didn't like Karadzic? Why?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What else?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the front line then and we received an order stating that Radovan Karadzic would arrive in Nevesinje and that we were supposed to go there to take part there so that there wouldn't be some incidents, right, by -- incidents caused by the Muslim army. As far as I heard, there weren't very many people in the streets when he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Did you state that Novica Gusic throughout the war received his salary from the JNA in Serbia, 1.000 Deutschemark per month?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Novica Gusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is what is on page 37 of your statement, the second paragraph there, that Novica Gusic throughout the war received from the JNA of Serbia a monthly salary of 1.000 Deutschemark. I know that this is science fiction, absolutely impossible, because I know what the salaries of officers in Serbia were.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the deputy commander was with me in the same battalion. He was also a military man from the JNA. He did not have a salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Buzina?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He had no salary?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In here it says that he got 300 Deutschemark from Serbia per month. How come that's in your statement?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the OTP do this?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe they commented upon that, that they got it from the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They could not get that much money?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come then?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know how come it's in your statement? Do you have the impression that the OTP inserted in your statement anything that came to their minds?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? I told you very nicely, the interpreter who was with this lady who was questioning me -- well, the two of them were speaking English, but I do speak a bit of English myself and they probably changed some expressions and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What about these people who attacked you the other day in Novi Sad and they beat you up; that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you defend yourself?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you injure any one of them?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I hit them but it wasn't really much of a blow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know any martial arts?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hardly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You never trained in any martial arts?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Diving, mountaineering, marksmanship, that's what I trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Karate and judo, no? Boxing, no?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way, boxing, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What about karate?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried karate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What about judo?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: See, in your statement on page 3 it says that you were good at martial arts in karate and judo. Did you actually say that to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I said mountaineering, fishing, marksmanship, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here it says karate and judo. And did you ever jump out of a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A helicopter? In Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From how high up?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say 15 -- no 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did you do that without getting hurt?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, that's not very high.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here it says that you jumped from an altitude of 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. I mean, I wouldn't jump into the water from 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let alone a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even from a helicopter into the water, 50 metres, no way. I didn't even jump off the Old Bridge in Mostar, let alone --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember the first killing that took place in Mostar just before the war started?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first killing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know Romeo Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He killed two Serb reservists?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As a member of the HOS?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's Paraga's unit?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was Blaz Kraljevic in command of that unit?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was killed by the Croats themselves?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Krusevo above Mostar in western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why did they kill him?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think because of some unsettled accounts, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Him and his escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They liquidated all of his escorts?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the road between Krusevo and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your father lost his life during the war in Mostar, right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from a Croat shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From a Croat shell?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, in September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. No, of course it's not very well. Unfortunately, he lost his life, but I'm just checking some data here.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May God rest his soul.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, I say the same thing. Now we reach the material that the OTP provided me with, a letter on the 25th of January. That's where the OTP said to me that already in 2002 you consider yourself to be in danger and that you asked to be relocated abroad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I really don't remember that I asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 27th of May, 2002, that is to say two years after that first interview you had with the OTP, did you have yet another interview in which you assessed the dangers that you were faced with? You talked to a (redacted) (redacted) I made a small mistake, so it's not from the OTP but the Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, for reasons you might well understand, we would ask that that name be redacted from the transcript or that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is totally wrong, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
