utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... we need to redact the name of the officer from the Victims and Witnesses Section, line 19, page 87.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What it says here is that you said that after having given a statement to the OTP in the winter of 2002 he felt isolated and was afraid that details of his connections with the International Criminal Tribunal might leak, and then the Serb authorities -- oh my goodness, what a miserable translation into Serbian. And then there is a mention of your then-code-name, that you mentioned that, and then that you kept changing your address and that you had moved seven or eight times by then. The witness also regularly changed the number of his mobile telephone. He was constantly in fear and did not feel safe. He didn't feel safe in Serbia or in Republika Srpska. The witness stated that he had trusted his old friends but there were other persons, and he mentioned them, who knew him and who might take the law into their own hands. That is what led to his concern for his own safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and the meeting took place on the 27th of May that year in the Bristol Hotel on the Neretva River in Mostar. The first thing that you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was before the indictment against me was issued?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who was it that endangered you, if you can say it in public session; if not, then forget it?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing secret about it. There was no danger coming from you. It had already become known that I had contacted the International Tribunal. There is no mention of you. I don't mention you, I mean, or any party, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could you when you didn't say anything bad about me in your first statement. I didn't see anything in the first statement that was bad for me.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't. I mean, when I met with that officer I didn't say that there was any danger coming from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever think that there was any danger coming from me when you gave the second statement?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From you, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Or men under my influence?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The person who talked to you says here: "The witness talked to a third person about what he got out of this," that is to say out of that evidence provided by you, "as if he were expecting some kind of a reward for his testimony." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So what does that mean, did you expect some kind of reward?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought that they would get me out to a third country somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that you had deserved that with that statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They also say: "The witness said that -- the statement says that the witness felt that his -- that he deserved a reward and" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The document is being read out too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then allegedly you were trying to assure him that that was not the case?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was mistranslated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were promises made to you during the first interview, that you could go to a foreign country?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And during the second interview in 2004 did they repeat that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I met with this -- this -- yes, Roy is his name. We talked and he said to me that they would no longer call me, that we had finished all our talks. But I said to him: I don't believe that, that you won't call me anymore, because I was in Sarajevo for two days down there in Nedzarici at the UN there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, he did call me again. I know that he'd call me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I got this from the OTP. I got it on the 26th of January this year, I got it just now before you came here. They mention here specifically 17 contacts that they had with you, and they say: "During the third contact on the 1st of December, 2002, that an investigator talked to you then," I'm not going to mention the name because otherwise we'll have to redact the transcript again. And then also there was counsel for the Prosecution. That's a prosecuting trial attorney. Can I mention that person's name, Judges, without you redacting the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tom Hannis. Do you remember that interview, that talk with Tom Hannis? It says here: "The witness was told that his request for relocation is being refused," that you were told that in December 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then they say: "The witness stated that he was disappointed by that fact and repeated questions related to his safety if he testifies in The Hague. Nevertheless, the witness did mention that he is still willing to co-operate with the OTP and that he would testify under full protective measures." Were you told at all in which trial you could testify then?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you were prepared to testify in any trial?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were never told in which trial?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. And they say that they refused your request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have about two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am just about to finish, Mr. President. I had to speed things up at the beginning. Now I can ask these questions with some ease which are not so important, but they enter into the merits of the behaviour of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 20th of February, 2008, you were called by the OTP and asked whether you would testify in this case. You said at the time that you wanted to be a witness for the Defence. And then that you said that actually you do not wish to testify for any party. And then you expressed the opinion that you were put in a highly vulnerable position by the driver, and then that the Court would send a summons for you to appear. Did you repeat your thesis that you were in danger in order to try to find for yourself shelter in a third country?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not repeat any such request at all. I told them nicely that whenever they called me that I wanted to be a witness of the Defence, and if you're interested there's something else that you may not know. They asked me to come here on the 15th of January and not on the 25th when it was scheduled. I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That isn't so important. I'm just checking what the OTP says about you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To end I'd like to ask the witness to look at this document which we've already shown during the hearing of some other witnesses. It has to do with Arsen Grahovac. The OTP has it and so does the Trial Chamber, and that will bring my cross-examination to an end.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we see the document before it's published?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a document whereby the president of Nevesinje municipality confirms that Arsen Grahovac was a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement until his death. You received that two years ago and you have that document. I showed that during the testimony of a protected witness, let me remind you, Judges, but I got this already in 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you look at it. Could you read it, please? It's short. This is chief Branislav Mikovic, you know him?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it issues a certificate. He refers to the general administrative procedure. Would you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took it away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Would you be so kind to give it to witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know English at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you speak perfect English, better English than I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Judge. That just appears to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you please read the text?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole text?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, just before -- underneath the word "certificate."

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. "Certificate, this is to certify that Grahovac, Blagoje, Arsen born on the 4th of January, 1955, in Nevesinje, as a candidate of the Serbian Renewal Movement was elected deputy to the Assembly of Nevesinje municipality at elections held on the 18th of November, 1990, and that he performed that duty until he was killed on the 22nd of August, 1992. "The certificate is being issued to be used as evidence that Grahovac, father's name Blagoje, first name Arsen, was a deputy of Nevesinje Municipal Assembly in the mentioned period as a candidate of the Serbian Renewal Movement, chief of the municipality Branislav Mikovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. The usher can pass on the document to members of the Trial Chamber, if you wish to have it, but I did give it to you two years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Biersay, you have five minutes, and I believe -- well, my fellow Judge had a question earlier, but I think she no longer has any questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Dabic, I'd like to understand exactly what it is that you're saying. Are you saying that in 2000, in November of 2000, an OTP investigator promised you on the spot that you would be taken to a third country in exchange for your statement? Is that what you're telling this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Simply, please. I have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- during the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- is -- yes or no, is that what you're telling the Trial Chamber? And then I'll ask another question depending on what you say.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you're saying that Brigitte Germain promised you that in exchange for your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that what you're saying --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I gave the statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- are you saying that she promised you relocation in exchange for your statement, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you nicely, after the conversation she said she would do everything she could.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So -- everything that she could. And what exactly did she tell you, you would have to do to be relocated?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it to be a promise, and all that I was supposed to do was to recount this period from the beginning until the end of the war what was happening in Mostar and eastern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did she tell you that you had to lie in your statement in order to get relocation to a third country?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't tell me to lie, but I keep saying that I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You have to listen closely to my questions. I have five minutes and I have been very efficient. Are you telling the Trial Chamber that you told lies in your 2000 statement? Is that what you're telling them?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said and told her --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- all the things I had heard and seen --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- I am asking you if you're telling this Trial Chamber that you lied in the 2000 statement that we have been looking at yesterday and today; is that what you're telling the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just -- I have just said that I didn't lie. That's out of the question. I was saying what I knew, what I heard, and what I had seen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, Judges. I think Ms. Biersay is trying to frighten the witness. I think the witness should be told that it -- he is not up for punishment if he tells lies to the Prosecution. He could be punished if he lies to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that would be a misrepresentation -- he would be lying here in the court and that would be a punishable offence, so that is incorrect legal advice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please rephrase your question because the -- maybe the witness did not understand it correctly. Could you please reformulate it and please speak slowly to make sure that the translation is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see a full question and full answer on the screen. I'm going to move to another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is important. Witness, you made a statement in 2000. When you made the statement, did you lie, yes or no? This is the question put to you by Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You did not lie. Does this mean that everything included in this November 2000 statement is true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you nicely in Serbian - and I'm repeating and you can understand because you have interpreters - I made this statement or statements according to what I had heard, what I had seen, and where I was present. So what I heard I really couldn't believe these things because I do not believe things that I don't see. What I saw I told them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must make another objection. The witness said repeatedly that he was surprised by certain sections even in the 2000 statement. It said, for instance, that he's good at martial arts, judo, karate, and that he jumped from a helicopter at a height of 50 metres. And now we are told that that is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is on the record. Ms. Biersay, please continue. He answered your question. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you met with the officer from the Victims and Witnesses Unit on the 27th May 2002, he specifically asked you whether or not the OTP had promised you anything, and you told him: "No, they have not." Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You were asked by the protection officer whether or not OTP had made any promises to you about relocation, and you told them -- you told him: "No, they have not made me any promises." Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, and if my brain is working properly I don't remember the officer asking me that. I don't know. This really was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this talk with the officer didn't last long.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Didn't the officer tell you that no one could make promises to you about relocation because of the appearance of it looking improper and it was not a proper thing to do, to make someone promises about relocation. Didn't he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating once again that I don't remember, but I do remember saying to him that I didn't feel safe in Serbia, where I was living --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That's a different question. I appreciate that. That was not my question. I am now asking you that between 2004 to 2007 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, you've run out of time, so just finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Between 2004 and 2007 did you ever file a report or tell anyone about misconduct on the -- on behalf of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 2004 and 2007?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Between 2004 and April of 2007.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dabic, on behalf of my fellow Judges -- my fellow didn't have a question but now she suddenly has one. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it came after an answer provided by the witness. He said that he did not feel safe. I would like to know why. Is it because you had lied that you didn't feel safe or is it because you had told the truth that you didn't feel safe?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think first of all I must repeat once again that I did not lie, that I said what I had heard and what I saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, witness, answer. It's either one or the other. You did not feel safe because you had lied; or option number two, you did not feel safe because you had told the truth? There are only two options. Why else wouldn't you feel safe after having made statements to the OTP of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV DABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I gave those statements that year, it had been learnt that I had given those statements, statements which were correct. And of course it's normal for me to have been afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. Witness, as I wanted to tell you, I would like to thank you to have come to testify on behalf of -- from the Trial Chamber, because you had been called by the Trial Chamber as a witness and you answered questions by the Trial Chamber, by the -- put to you by the Prosecution, and by Mr. Seselj. I wish you a safe return home, and I would like to ask our usher to escort you out of this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before closing I have a very brief administrative issue to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll deal with this after the witness has left the courtroom. You may leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Procedural questions, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to tire you with any written submissions. On the 22nd of January, 2010, I received from the OTP the public document to accept -- to admit into evidence P00019, 326, 327, and 328, and the OTP is requesting in an addendum that my speech of the 4th of September in 1989 should be admitted into evidence. And they say that I held this speech in the St. Nicolas Serbian Orthodox church in Hamilton in Canada. Then again my speech of the 4th of September, the same place. I just wanted to let you know that on the 4th of September, 1989, I was not in Canada. In September 1989, end of August, September, and beginning of October I was on a tour of Great Britain, France, Germany, Switzerland, and again I went back to Great Britain. I was not in Canada in August or in October or in July or in November, in June or December, and this can be verified with the Canadian immigration authorities. The speech may have been truthful, but at that time I was not in Canada. I just wanted to inform you of this without tiring you with a written submission about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will look into these documents. I don't know exactly where we stand. It seems -- these documents seem to say that you made a speech when you were in Canada, but you're saying that you were not in Canada.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President, I was in Canada, but not on that date, neither was I there three months before that or three months after that. In September I simply was not in Canada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, the Trial Chamber was seized of a request for an MFI number for documents P880. Let me make sure on the screen that it's well transcribed. P880, P881, P882, P883, and P884.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are all witness statements, are they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just to be precise, the Prosecution is only asking for the admission of P880 and P881, which I believe are the 2000 and 2004 statements respectively. We are not seeking the admission of the others.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I express my position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, Judges, that in principle I am opposed to the admission of statements by witnesses, either to the Prosecution or the Defence. The Anglo-Saxon law does not recognise such a procedure. It is impossible according to Anglo-Saxon law. In European continental law it is also impossible. In European law you may make a statement before an investigating judge, and that may be admitted into evidence if the defence was present during the hearing. And if the prosecutor is conducting the investigation, again the defence must be present and have the possibility to examine. But anything taken by the Prosecution without the presence of the defence or taken by the police without the presence of the defence or if the witness renounces the right to the presence of counsel cannot be admitted into evidence. I'm in a dilemma now. In principle I am against, but intimately it would suit my interest for both those documents to be admitted because they illustrate the behaviour of the OTP. I hope you heard my last sentence. And they put it in a very bad light.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did hear because whilst we were talking among ourselves I was listening to you. We are very well aware of this problem you have addressed previously. After discussing the matter, the Trial Chamber decides to admit five statements. The first statement was made to the Prosecution on the 10th of November, 2000, it will be P880. Second statement, statement to the Prosecution on the 9th and 10th of June, 2004, it will be P881. Third statement to the Defence, on the 11th of May, 2007, it will be P882. Fourth statement to the Defence on the 7th of June, 2007, it will be P883. And the Trial Chamber also admits the fifth statement that was made to the Defence on the 14th of October, 2008, it will be P884. Next week we are scheduled to have a witness on Tuesday and Wednesday. Apparently there's no problem about it if I remember well. It should be Witness VS-1067, a Chamber witness from memory. I may be mistaken, but I believe that the Judges are going to use an hour and a half, same amount of time for the Prosecution and also for Mr. Seselj. I mean, this is what I remember. It might be one hour -- no, it's one hour and 30 minutes. Yes, this has just been confirmed by the Legal Officer. Very well. So an hour and a half for the Judges, an hour and a half for the Prosecution, and the same amount of time for the -- for Mr. Seselj. And as usual, we're going to share the load among ourselves, each Judge using 30 minutes. Oh, thank you, Mr. Registrar. Regarding the schedule -- thank you, Mr. Registrar, because the Legal Officer was wrong, but nothing escapes the Registrar's attention. We have a decision of the 8th of December, 2009, regarding VS-1067. It was scheduled to be one hour. So one hour for the questions by the Judges, one hour for the Prosecution, and one hour for the Defence represented by Mr. Seselj himself. So it was one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Very quickly, I believe Mr. Marcussen has an issue to address to the Court, but with respect to the testimony of the previous witness, the Prosecution will move for the admission of the certificate that Mr. Seselj showed the witness, and that is 65 ter number 1636, and we would also move now for the admission of 65 ter number 1910, which discusses the certificate that Mr. Seselj showed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, I suppose you do not object to having this document you used admitted into evidence? Mr. Registrar, let's have a number for the document, for the 1910.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1636 will be Exhibit P888, and 65 ter number 0910 will be Exhibit P889.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's 1910.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I stand corrected, 65 ter 0910 will be Exhibit P889.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1910 will be 889.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is going to be P889. Yes, Mr. Marcussen, we have three minutes left. What do you have to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the accused has made an oral response to the motion that was filed by the Prosecution on the 20th of January this year. He has asserted, as he did earlier on, when these videos that the motion concern were shown, that he was not in Canada at the time. The Prosecution has provided arguments as to why the videos were taken at the location that we say they were taken. If the accused wants to provide evidence in support of his view that he was not in Canada at this point in time, he should do so, but he cannot just assert in court that he -- well, he can just assert in court that he was not in Canada at the relevant time. But really, he should obtain evidence to support this claim if he wants to make it, otherwise he hasn't done anything other than simply making an assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have taken due note of what Mr. Seselj has said and of what you said. Of course, the Trial Chamber will rule on this. Thank you. I want to thank everybody. We shall reconvene next week on Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of February, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
